dedupe_keys.name: gaza strip sar based spatial analysis of damage to health education and water facilities 7 october to 22 november 2023

description: This study maps damage to health, education and water facilities across the Gaza Strip during the first phase of the Israeli military campaign, from 7 October to 22 November 2023. Yara Asi, David Mills, P. Gregg Greenough and co-authors published it in Conflict and Health in April 2024. They applied multi-temporal coherent change detection to Copernicus Sentinel-1 radar imagery to detect damage to the built environment, located facilities from open building footprints checked against OCHA, OpenStreetMap and Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team data, and tested clustering with Global Moran's I. They found 60.8 percent of health, 68.2 percent of education and 42.1 percent of water facilities damaged, with about 35 to 40 percent functionally destroyed, and damage significantly clustered around all three types. Coverage is the Gaza Strip. Format and access: an open access article with supplementary material. Licence: CC-BY-4.0 for the article; free. Caveats: radar change detection flags damage near facilities, not confirming it building by building, and the paper also argues legal questions beyond infrastructure analysis. It documents a method for rapid hazard exposure assessment of critical facilities in conflict. Related catalogue records are the attacks on hospitals in Gaza dataset and the Gaza electricity distribution damage assessment.
